newsitem.title: UK: UK SIB says 102 mln stg paid in pensions redress.
newsitem.headline: UK SIB says 102 mln stg paid in pensions redress.

text.p: Britain's financial watchdog, the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) said on Tuesday that 102 million stg has already been paid out to investors who were wrongly sold pensions in the pensions misselling scandal.
It said some 12,650 people have accepted offers of redress, working out to an average of 8,000 stg per investor.
Earlier, the SIB announced further measures to speed up the review of the misselling which has been going on since 1994.
As part of the measures, the SIB and Personal Investment Authority, the front-line regulator, said they will take steps to increase investor awareness of the review.
The SIB has produced a new investor factsheet which explains how the review of pensions misselling works and what investors need to do to ensure that their case is considered for redress.
"Our publicity programme is designed to coincide with the mailing of questionnaires by firms to investors. Unless investors reply, their cases cannot be considered for redress," the SIB said.

The companies most heavily involved in the pensions industry are due to meet Economic Secretary to the Treasury Helen Liddell on Wednesday. She is expected to put pressure on them to complete the review and compensate the victims.
